title: Model 2 coast-reach probabilities: calibrated on drifters
scope: Probability that a drifting object crosses a stretch of line within a lead time, from a forecast track plus empirical error paths, tested across two historical periods.
summary: At 48 h the error-path ensemble scored Brier 0.00657 and 0.00663 across the two cross-period directions, versus 0.00687 and 0.00681 for a Gaussian spread, 0.00958 and 0.00960 for the single forecast track, and 0.01025 and 0.01022 for climatology (Brier skill versus climatology about 0.35 to 0.36). At 120 h: 0.0182 and 0.0184 versus Gaussian 0.0194 and 0.0192 (skill 0.24). Forecast probabilities matched observed frequencies across the range, for example forecasts of 0.55 came true 55% of the time at 48 h. The single track is overconfident and worse than climatology beyond about 72 h.

metrics.name: Error-path ensemble Brier, 48 h
metrics.provenance: Earlier-period errors applied to the development period; other direction 0.00663.

limitations: The source report is an untracked working-tree file; it is identified by SHA-256 only and has no source commit.
Historical undrogued surface drifters, not Sargassum mats; live calibration for Sargassum must be checked separately.
Analysis fields stand in for forecasts, and both periods were used in earlier development, so this is cross-period rather than prospective.
The gain over a simple Gaussian spread is small (about 3 to 7 percent lower Brier).
Discrimination (AUC 0.92 to 0.99) is inflated by many easy distant segments; Brier skill is the meaningful measure.
